name: Directional Solidification
desc: An alloy pulled through a thermal gradient: the flat freezing front is unstable, so it buckles into an array of cells whose tips race ahead into richer liquid while surface tension fights back, and the array never settles - cells split, drift and get squeezed out in Kuramoto-Sivashinsky chaos as the selected spacing wanders; the solid keeps the record, so the cell grooves trail away downward as the microstructure with the pulling rate laying horizontal bands through it, read as a false-colour phase field, an etched longitudinal section, Nomarski relief, or a blueprint of groove trajectories.

energy.doc: contrast, front amplitude and the latent-heat glow behind the interface

scale.doc: magnification into the section - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: pulling rate and front dynamics - how fast the microstructure scrolls away (0.2 still grows)

density.doc: selected cell spacing - a few broad cells vs a fine dense array across the front

band.doc: how hard the pulling rate is modulated - depth of the banded microstructure laid into the solid

hue.doc: hue of the solid; the melt takes its complement

x.doc: pan across the section when magnified

y.doc: pan along the growth direction when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: false-colour phase field with hot mushy zone / etched longitudinal metallographic section / Nomarski differential-interference relief / blueprint of groove trajectories
